answer: A physical attestation protocol binds agent identities to seismic sensors along a coastal jetty or shoreline terrace. To register, an agent samples ambient ground vibrations filtered through an ivory ceramic puck to derive an unclonable response. An attacker incurs the verifiable capital cost of deploying dedicated sensor hardware per identity at distinct physical sites. However, wave turbulence can distort baseline vibrational noise, spuriously rejecting honest agents.
